title_original: Hoor Al-Qasimi Appointed Curator for 2028 Venice Biennale
excerpt_original: She will be the first Arab curator to helm the prestigious international art exhibition. HARISON BUTLER

blocks.text: Hoor Al-Qasimi Appointed Curator for 2028 Venice Biennale

blocks.alt: Hoor Al-Qasimi Appointed Curator for 2028 Venice Biennale

blocks.text: HOOR AL-QASIMI . Photo by Chieska Fortune Smith.

The Board of La Biennale di Venezia has appointed Hoor Al-Qasimi , president and director of the Sharjah Art Foundation (SAF), to curate the 62nd Venice Biennale in 2028. She will be the first Arab curator of the international art exhibition.

Al-Qasimi has been active in the international contemporary art world for over two decades. The Emirati curator has led major exhibitions such as the 2020 Lahore Biennale, the 2025 Aichi Triennale, and the 2026 Biennale of Sydney. She has led the Sharjah Biennial since 2003 and, in 2009, founded SAF, which supports contemporary art and cultural exchange in Sharjah and abroad. Since 2017, she has been president of the International Biennial Association. She is also president and director of the Sharjah Architecture Triennial, which was launched in 2019 by her late brother Khalid Al-Qasimi.

Pietrangelo Buttafuoco, president of the Venice Biennale, recommended Al-Qasimi for the role, explaining, “Her work brings together a profound attentiveness to deep-rooted memory and its legacies, an open perspective on the intricate complexities of the present, and a rare ability to listen to places and their people. . . . These are qualities that we feel are particularly close to [the Biennale’s] vision.” In a statement, Al-Qasimi thanked the board and said the Venice Biennale “has been an important platform for many of us around the world. . . . For me, [it] continues to be a critical space to engage with the work of influential artists and curators.”
In our 145 issue , we profiled Al-Qasimi , tracing her numerous curatorial endeavors and sustained engagement with non-Western artists.
Harison Butler is an editorial intern at ArtAsiaPacific.
